task_summary: Implement balanced-bracket checking in solution.py, add unittest regression coverage, and document design decisions and a verification command in HANDOFF.md.
constraints: Work only in the supplied task workspace.
Edit solution.py and public tests; HANDOFF.md is an allowed output.
Use Python 3.11+ and the standard library.
Do not access parent repositories or external services.
Check nesting of (), [] and {}; ignore other characters; unmatched opening or closing brackets return false; empty text returns true.
Maintain type hints and do not mutate input collections.
No algorithmic complexity constraint is imposed.
test_solution.py must contain at least 3 passing unittest test methods exercising the public API.
HANDOFF.md must include design decisions and the verification command.

success_criteria.description: test_solution.py exists and contains at least three unittest test methods.

check.command: python -c 'import ast; from pathlib import Path; tree = ast.parse(Path("test_solution.py").read_text()); assert sum(isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name.startswith("test") for cls in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(cls, ast.ClassDef) for n in cls.body) >= 3'

success_criteria.description: The public unittest suite completes successfully with the requested discovery command.
HANDOFF.md includes design decisions and the requested verification command.

assumptions: The requested files are interpreted as relative paths in the supplied workspace; solution.py, test_solution.py, and HANDOFF.md may not exist yet and may be created.
The public API name and signature are unspecified, so tests should exercise the API implemented in solution.py without assuming a particular name or signature.

The phrase “at least 3 passing unittest test methods” is checked structurally for at least three test-prefixed methods in unittest.TestCase subclasses; successful discovery is checked separately for execution.
The HANDOFF.md requirement is interpreted as including the exact requested verification command and a section or text explicitly identifying design decisions.
